title: Chicago immediately before the fire — 1871 reconstruction research
scope: Prepare Chicago for October 8, 1871 before the evening outbreak, with the exact local hour still open. An October 7 intact-city baseline is a separate state: Sunday already includes damage from the Saturday Night Fire.

cards.title: Original Chamber: source images and conflicting dimensions
cards.statement: The acquired Chicago Illustrated plate and companion text identify the original 1865 building. The contemporary text gives 93 × 181 feet and 100 feet in height without a height datum. Andreas’s retrospective 1885 account gives 93 × 180 feet and prints both the roof extreme and cornice at 99 feet above the basement floor while also giving a 23-foot roof rise. This is a real printed contradiction, not an OCR error.
cards.applies_to: Original Chamber completed August 28 and dedicated August 30, 1865; destroyed in October 1871. Exact destruction time is not established here.
cards.render_implication: The reusable plate is now inspectable in the notebook with its full margins and scan provenance. Reconstruct the visible portal, upper arch rhythm, quoins, cornice and mansard through a solved camera; make any selected height/depth an explicit inference or reconstruction.
cards.limits: Andreas wrote retrospectively in 1885; the plate and companion text were published in 1866–67. The engraving caption “CHAMBER OF COMMERCE.” does not date its creation; surrounding text and the matching facade identify the original phase. Neither image is a survey or October 8 witness. The CHM digital poster remains restricted; the displayed plate was independently obtained from the PD HathiTrust/University of Michigan scan through Commons. These sources do not yet supply a completed reconstruction.
cards.next_step: Choose a working depth and vertical profile with stated bounds and confidence, preserving both source reports. Reconcile the period parcel; unpictured faces and uncertain details may be reconstructed with their reasoning recorded.

Historic Pine does not inherit modern widened Michigan Avenue curb geometry. The inspected CHM Pine Street photograph is restricted and is not published here.

cards.title: Municipal bridge inventory and baseline crossings
cards.statement: The report’s 27 named rows reconcile with its 16 iron-chord/wooden-brace, one all-iron and ten wooden-bridge categories. The current foundation plan represents 21 of those rows and explicitly omits Erie, Twenty-second, Main, Fuller, Archer and Western. Its separately map-backed Division Street canal crossing makes 22 rendered road crossings. The difference follows the baseline’s documented scope.
cards.applies_to: Report evidence through spring 1871; baseline plan inspected November 19, 2026.
cards.render_implication: Keep rendered crossings, dated report inventory and explicit omissions separate. Preserve stable identities when resolving an omitted crossing.
cards.limits: Erie and Twenty-second were “Not in use” in the March traffic-count context; October openings remain unresolved. Four other rows lack confidently matched period-map placements. Western’s 1869 “W. fork of S. Branch” table row and the narrative’s new canal bridge require identity work; “No account” is not “Not in use”. Traffic arithmetic and the complete private/railway/October inventory were not verified.
cards.next_step: Resolve the six existing omissions individually; do not change placements or operational status from counts alone.

cards.title: J. C. Alexander, a carpenter linked to McVicker’s
cards.statement: Edwards’ 1871 directory lists J. C. Alexander as a carpenter associated with McVicker’s Theatre, residing at historical 75 Huron. The theatre list puts McVicker’s on Madison between Dearborn and State. This is a distinct entry from the William Alexander waiter and drayman.
cards.applies_to: 1871 directory compilation; no exact canvass date, October 8 presence or 16:00 activity is established.
cards.render_implication: Use the listed identity and occupation for a future evidence card. Appearance, clothing, exact position and any exterior routine require separate reconstructed choices and clear walk support.
cards.limits: Do not expand the initials or infer age, race, tools, household, payroll status, exact duties, shift, commute, stage work or a performance. Neither the historic residence number nor the workplace corridor supplies modern coordinates. No person, portrait or routine is created by this research pass.
cards.next_step: Match the historical theatre frontage and street surfaces before proposing an explicitly reconstructed depiction.

cards.title: Vegetation needs habitat evidence before species precision
cards.statement: Verified sources establish broad land use, wetness, disturbance, drought, cemetery retention, and tree condition, but not a citywide 1871 species or planting-density inventory. The 1870 Board report now provides specific local planting evidence: large elms and shrubbery in Lincoln Park, and deciduous and evergreen trees in Union Park. cards.title: Court House and City Hall: the enlarged pre-fire building
cards.statement: The 1853 combined Court House and City Hall occupied the block bounded by Randolph, Clark, Washington and LaSalle, with landscaped grounds around its relatively small footprint. cards.statement: The Chamber of Commerce dedicated Edward Burling's building at the southeast corner of Washington and LaSalle on August 30, 1865. cards.title: Sherman House: six-story pre-fire hotel
cards.statement: The pre-fire replacement Sherman House was a six-story hotel designed by W. W. Boyington and faced with local limestone described as Athens Marble. Its main entrance faced Clark Street through a two-story portico. cards.applies_to: 1871-10-08 before the Great Fire
cards.render_implication: Research the portico, stone stair, façade rhythm and relationship to Court House Square using ichi-00761. Hotel loading, luggage and carriage arrivals are possible action systems but need their own evidence.
cards.limits: Do not use the 1858 predecessor, 1873 rebuilding, circa-1890 photograph or 1911 hotel as interchangeable façade references.

cards.statement: The pre-fire Field & Leiter store stood at the northeast corner of State and Washington. cards.statement: Crosby's stood on the north side of Washington between State and Dearborn. The five-story Italianate front with a mansard roof housed shops, offices and an art gallery; the auditorium was behind it. Renovations occurred in summer 1871 and a reopening concert was scheduled for October 9, after the fire began.

cards.statement: The museum describes a double cottage: the O'Learys and their five children occupied the rear section, while the McLaughlin family rented the front. cards.title: Edwards' 1871 directory: extracted addresses, occupations and uses
cards.statement: The original 1871 Edwards directory has now been read selectively: apparatus, alarm locations, congregations, railway schedules, street numbering, public buildings, residents, florists, stables, food and ice businesses. Page-level observations and original scans are available in the field notebook.
cards.applies_to: Directory publication and canvass period in 1871; not a guaranteed October 8 census
cards.render_implication: Connect listed businesses and residents to evidence-backed building entities; use listings to prioritize signage and activity research without treating every listing as a separate structure.
cards.limits: A directory is neither a complete population census nor proof of construction date. Modern address numbers and same-name post-fire businesses cannot be substituted without a crosswalk.
cards.next_step: Join selected historical addresses to period parcel maps; independently resolve footprint, elevation, facade and exact-date occupancy. Expand extraction by block, preserving omissions and conflicting listings.

cards.title: Population: use the census as a baseline, not a street crowd count
cards.statement: The 1870 federal census counted 298,977 Chicago residents. Illinois State Archives reports 144,557 foreign-born residents, or 48.35 percent. These are citywide counts from the year before the fire, not a count of people present on October 8, 1871.
cards.applies_to: Citywide population context; 1870 census baseline for the 1871 scene
cards.render_implication: Build a varied population rather than a uniform frontier-town crowd. Separate resident population, commuters, visitors, street occupancy, indoor occupancy, and time of day. Citywide demographic proportions do not determine the composition of every block.
cards.limits: The census does not directly specify October 1871 street density, clothing, spoken language, or the appearance of particular people.
cards.next_step: Extract ward-level census tables and selected household schedules; pair them with dated addresses before assigning local population weights.

cards.title: Resolve demographic classifications before creating exact quotas
cards.statement: Published summaries disagree on some detailed counts. The Illinois Archives table lists Germany as 59,299, while the Ninth Census Compendium's indexed Germany column reports 52,318; other birthplaces have their own columns. Such differences must be reconciled against the actual table headings and definitions rather than silently combined.
cards.applies_to: Foreign-birth classifications and demographic documentation
cards.render_implication: Keep birthplace, nationality, language, race, occupation, and costume as distinct fields. Do not infer a person's ethnicity from clothing or apply a modern national boundary to a historical census category.
cards.limits: The Compendium PDF text was read, but its dense table OCR is unreliable and screenshot extraction failed. The detailed counts are not approved for production quotas.

cards.title: Include Black Chicagoans without importing the later Great Migration city
cards.statement: The National Park Service reports a Black population of 3,691 in Chicago in 1870. Other historical summaries round this to about 3,700 or 4,000. This establishes an existing community before the fire, not a population that arrived only in the twentieth century. The original 1871 directory additionally locates Quinn Chapel at Jackson/Fourth avenue, Bethel on Third avenue, and Olivet on Fourth between Taylor and Polk, with named ministers and Sunday schedules.
cards.applies_to: People and community research for 1871
cards.render_implication: Include Black residents in the research and actor inventory. Determine households, businesses, institutions, and occupations through specific records rather than assigning generic servant roles or importing twentieth-century Bronzeville geography.
cards.limits: The exact census count needs page-level reconciliation because some other summaries report 3,696. This source does not establish a particular person's street location or appearance on October 8.
cards.next_step: Use these institution-specific pages to resolve pre-fire parcels and images, then trace named households and businesses through census and directory records. Keep the unresolved population-table discrepancy separate from these documented institutions.

cards.title: 1871 horsecar schedules refine the earlier route baseline
cards.statement: The 1871 directory p. 53 supplies a contemporary timetable: State/Randolph to 22d every minute, Cottage Grove services every four minutes, Archer every eight, selected North Side services every twelve or fifteen, Graceland hourly, and several West Side services every five. These are nominal service descriptions; the earlier 1870 comparison must retain its own date.
cards.applies_to: Transport network baseline immediately preceding 1871
cards.render_implication: Create route-constrained vehicle paths, terminals and waiting locations. The same source lists a 2½-minute State Street headway to Twenty-second Street; treat that as a dated timetable attribute, not a universal spawning interval.
cards.limits: A nominal timetable does not establish Sunday frequency, actual October 8 headways, complete track geometry, simultaneous vehicle totals or car capacity.
cards.next_step: Resolve named route endpoints and track alignments on period maps and seek Sunday service notices; retain the 1870 source only as a dated comparison.

cards.title: A surviving Chicago horsecar provides a measured comparison
cards.statement: Illinois Railway Museum records North Chicago Street Railroad 8 as a single-truck, Bombay-roof horsecar with 18 seats, hand brakes, and listed dimensions of 12 feet long, 7 feet 5 inches wide, and 9 feet 6 inches high. Its driver stood on the front platform; one or two horses hauled it.
cards.applies_to: Horsecar asset research
cards.render_implication: Use this compact vehicle as a dimensional comparison and model the exposed driver, horse coupling and hand-brake operation. Confirm what the listed length measures before building a complete envelope.
cards.limits: The museum prints its construction year as '1859?' and says the car was rebuilt for the 1933 Century of Progress exhibition. Current fabric and dimensions cannot automatically certify its exact 1871 condition or the whole fleet.
cards.next_step: Compare the museum photographs and dimensions against dated Chicago street photographs and builder drawings; record any reconstruction explicitly.

cards.title: Horse traffic requires stables and care, not just moving animals
cards.statement: The museum's horsecar history describes the support burden of horse traction: food, water, hostlers, veterinary care and manure. Exact stable operations in an 1871 Chicago block need separate records.
cards.applies_to: Street railways, drayage, omnibuses, private carriages and service yards
cards.render_implication: Create linked care actions: harnessing, unhitching, watering, feeding, grooming, resting and cleaning. Place them only where an appropriate yard, stable, water source and access route exist.
cards.limits: These are proposed behavior systems, not witnessed actions at a particular time or proof of stable locations. Do not model all horses as identical or make every horse continuously work.
cards.next_step: Use the notebook’s named stables and feed dealers as address anchors; locate yards, doors, water and manure access from parcel sheets. The 1870 report attests public animal troughs but does not locate each one.

cards.title: The river needs commercial schooners as well as steam vessels
cards.statement: Chicago Maritime Museum describes the city's grain and lumber trades as heavily dependent on schooners, with lumber arriving from Michigan and Wisconsin. It identifies Wolf Point as a location where arriving lumber cargoes were inspected and sold.
cards.applies_to: River, docks, grain elevators, lumber yards and harbor approaches
cards.render_implication: Distinguish inbound lumber cargo, outbound grain, docked vessels, and vessels under way. Represent the commercial chain with cargo-specific berths and destinations rather than distributing decorative boats uniformly.
cards.limits: The museum gives broad traffic magnitudes, not an October 8 vessel manifest. Its port-ranking claims should not become exact simultaneous vessel counts.
cards.next_step: Acquire dated arrival/clearance columns, vessel registers, berth photographs and insurance-map waterfront facilities; name ships only after confirming their presence.

cards.title: Use Great Lakes schooner forms rather than ocean-ship defaults
cards.statement: Chicago Public Library describes wooden centerboard schooners with fore-and-aft rigs as characteristic Lake Michigan cargo craft. Centerboards helped them navigate shallow harbor bars; the fore-and-aft rig could be handled by comparatively small crews.
cards.applies_to: Comparative vessel morphology
cards.render_implication: Research hull proportions, centerboard cases, masts, booms, rigging, cargo stowage and working decks. Distinguish furled sails at a berth from a sailing configuration and obtain specific evidence for towing or maneuvering.
cards.limits: This is a regional type description, not proof of a named vessel, exact hull dimensions, sail state or berth on October 8.
cards.next_step: Choose a documented vessel or narrowly defined class and connect its plan to a dated Chicago image.

cards.title: Animate commodity handling as linked tasks
cards.statement: The documented grain, lumber, hotel-transfer and livestock economies support a research program for freight labor. The precise motions below are reconstruction proposals until matched to a workplace and period technique.
cards.applies_to: Wharves, warehouses, freight depots, lumber yards and commercial streets
cards.render_implication: Create task sequences with props and destinations: inspect cargo, handle lines, move a load, stack material, receive delivery, record a transaction, and return equipment. Each sequence should require a compatible cart, load, doorway, platform, ramp or berth.
cards.limits: Do not assume every task occurred on Sunday, every commodity used sacks or barrels, every dock had the same lifting machinery, or every worker had the same occupation and clothing.
cards.next_step: Attach each proposed action to a dated image, trade manual, newspaper description, business record or surviving tool before marking it documented.

cards.title: Separate livestock-market activity from downtown street life
cards.statement: The Union Stock Yard and Transit Company was incorporated in 1865 to consolidate stockyard operations. This is a major economic system to research, but its site and transport links must be represented separately from downtown commerce.
cards.applies_to: Southern industrial and livestock districts; regional economic context
cards.render_implication: If the modeled extent reaches the stockyards, investigate pens, gates, watering, feeding, weighing, rail loading and animal movement. For a downtown-only extent, show only locally evidenced supply and transport connections.
cards.limits: Published summaries describe different acreages for different dates or definitions. Do not project the later, much-expanded stockyards, later gate, or mature refrigerated-meat system backward into 1871.
cards.next_step: Read the incorporating act and a dated 1871 yard plan; establish the scene boundary before commissioning yard assets.

cards.title: A documented household dairy links residents, animals and work
cards.statement: Chicago History Museum identifies Catherine O'Leary as a local milk seller whose barn held five cows and a horse. The O'Learys and five children occupied the rear of a double cottage; the McLaughlin family rented the front.
cards.applies_to: O'Leary property on DeKoven Street; comparative household-economy research
cards.render_implication: Research shared occupancy, rear-yard access, dairy animals, storage and household work. Milk handling, animal care and deliveries are possible reconstructed routines, requiring separately verified implements and timing.
cards.limits: This establishes a specific household economy, not that every urban yard kept cows. The museum explicitly identifies the cow-and-lamp origin scene as mythic; do not depict it as witnessed fact. The cited cottage stereograph is from 1871 after the fire.
cards.next_step: Compare the cottage image, lot records, census household and inquiry testimony; distinguish surviving cottage evidence from speculative barn geometry.

cards.title: Date clothing from object records and distinguish comparison from local proof
cards.statement: The Metropolitan Museum catalogs an American wool-and-cotton suit dated 1870–73, object 2009.300.7719a–e, and an American silk dress dated 1870–73, object 1979.346.113a,b. Both records provide public-domain collection images.
cards.applies_to: Comparative clothing materials, cut and construction
cards.render_implication: Build reference sheets with front, side and back views, garment components, fabric and provenance. Use the records as period comparators, then match attire to role, wealth, age, weather and activity through local evidence.
cards.limits: Neither catalog establishes a Chicago wearer in October 1871. Date ranges can include later manufacture. The suit's garment type and intended wearer require visual inspection before assigning it to an actor. Museum survival favors certain garments over ordinary working clothes.
cards.next_step: Inspect all object photographs and local dated portraits or street images; source working clothes, headwear, footwear, children's clothing and repairs separately.

cards.title: October 8 was Sunday: schedules need a date, not just a year
cards.statement: The museum timeline dates the fire's beginning to Sunday, October 8, 1871. Crosby's Opera House was scheduled to reopen on October 9 after refurbishment; that planned concert never took place.
cards.applies_to: Scene calendar and cultural activity
cards.render_implication: Make weekday/Sunday, hour and event status explicit inputs. Worship, visiting, recreation and transport should be researched against Sunday schedules. Do not populate Crosby's with an audience for the unrealized October 9 reopening.
cards.limits: Sunday does not prove all shops were closed or that all residents attended church. Churchgoing, visiting and leisure actions remain reconstruction choices until tied to local services or testimony.
cards.next_step: Use the extracted Sunday service times as schedule evidence, then consult October 8 notices to verify actual events. A timetable or monthly society rule is not an eyewitness record of attendance.

cards.title: Immediately before the Great Fire was already after another major fire
cards.statement: The museum timeline places the Saturday Night Fire on October 7 in the area bounded by Van Buren, Clinton, Adams and the South Branch. It reports twenty destroyed buildings and firefighting continuing into October 8 afternoon, leaving crews exhausted and equipment needing repair.

cards.limits: The chronology does not provide parcel-level damage, exact surviving structures, smoke opacity or the location of each crew at a chosen hour.
cards.next_step: Digitize the earlier fire footprint from contemporary reporting and compare it with the intended scene time; distinguish this damage from the subsequent Great Fire.

cards.title: Operational rules offer behavior constraints without proving compliance
cards.statement: The museum timeline records a January 30, 1871 request to enforce the six-mile-per-hour city train-speed limit, and a January 24 order extending station-tower fire watches from nightfall until 9:30 p.m., when the regular night watch began.
cards.applies_to: Rail crossings, stations and fire-watch behavior
cards.render_implication: Treat rail crossings as shared conflict points and investigate watchtower sightlines. Store legal speed limits separately from reconstructed movement speed and actual observed compliance.
cards.limits: A rule documents an intended practice, not universal obedience or the exact roster on October 8. This does not specify locomotive type, track elevation or every watchtower's geometry.
cards.next_step: Find the original council and fire-commission records, dated track maps, apparatus inventories and station locations.

cards.title: Every populated scene needs an action-and-prop evidence record
cards.statement: The researched sources establish people, vehicles, commodities, premises and dated events at different levels of specificity. They do not jointly establish a fully observed street scene at a single moment. Animation requires an explicit reconstruction layer.
cards.applies_to: All people, animals and moving vehicles
cards.render_implication: For each action record actor role, location, time window, destination, required props, motion constraints, source, confidence and exclusions. Useful candidate routines include walking, waiting, boarding, alighting, carrying luggage, receiving goods, tending animals, shopping, visiting, handling dock lines and recording transactions.
cards.limits: These are proposed authoring requirements and candidate actions, not a claim that each occurred at the chosen location and moment. Keep named historical people separate from anonymous reconstructed actors.
cards.next_step: Choose one documented block, wharf and residential lot as pilots. Build complete actor–prop–place chains and expose unresolved evidence before expanding crowd density.

year_audit.status: Implemented scene; released flag remains false
year_audit.summary: First Fort Dearborn on natural ground before the harbor cut. Current indexes contain 68 structure/component entries, 834 people records and 284 standalone human instances; these are dataset units, not simultaneous visible counts.
lessons: Use an exact day and independent terrain state. The pre-cut mouth, sand spit and natural banks have their own derived geometry; remove later streets, piers and bridges explicitly.
Keep buildings, outer compounds, gardens, enclosures, yard goods and crossings separately inspectable. Camera anchors let reviewers test the same places repeatedly.

Current routines support 284 drawn and 520 callable residents, with dates, seasons, duties, work, conversations, play, meals and indoor periods. These schedules and rendering limits are declared liberties.
Keep identity, presence, appearance and action separate. A named person is not evidence for their exact face, outfit or minute-by-minute behavior.
Reuse the day engine, door access, spacing and route systems for 1871; research new households, occupations, clothes and routes. Do not carry 1812 ground or individual placements forward.
The scene note mentioning only one soldier is stale. Current human indexes and the routines dossier establish the later implementation.

year_audit.summary: The broadest existing settlement layer inventory: 687 structure/component sidecars and 3,891 people-directory entries, including 307 transients. Four standalone instances and a wagon route demonstrate actors; the directory is not a street crowd.
lessons: Research all layers: land, water, ordinary buildings, streets, fences, signs, goods, gardens, frontage, wharves, boats, wells, businesses, people, horses and lights.
Use slow terrain epochs and faster dated structure phases. Resolve exactly one phase on the target date and compile that historical decision into the sidecar.
Preserve natural habitat, planted ground, bare soil and strata separately. Areal cover and stems per square metre are different units.
Fauna distinguish seen, heard, trace-only, absent and undepicted presence. July species/activity records cannot automatically represent October 1871.
People records distinguish home, work, presence, dated roles, reconstructed households and transients. Apply new 1871 sources rather than carrying old trade shares and names.
Use aggregate totals to constrain explicitly reconstructed ordinary fabric; never turn them into individually documented addresses.
Night-light records separate evidence for candles/oil from reconstructed brightness, window-hour shares and exact placements.

year_audit.status: Implemented Prairie Avenue scene; released flag remains false
year_audit.summary: A parcel-scale urban model with 284 structure/component sidecars, 445 directory records and eight standalone human instances. The separate research library has 63 named building records, 138 sources, 38 maps and 73 occupancy candidates.
lessons: Distinguish source map date from scene date: 1911 frontage readings are explicitly adjudicated for 1904, and the 1886/1911 shoreline bounds remain visible.
Count front buildings, wings, rear buildings, shared coach houses and service parcels separately. Name continuity does not prove unchanged fabric.
Use street sections, curbs, walks, alleys, front and rear yards, railways, trees, lamps, hydrants, poles and wires as dated urban infrastructure.
Combine rule-based tree placement with picture-specific overrides; an empty photographed interval can rule a tree out.
Use independent camera and façade evidence, preserving uncertainty in ground and shoreline. A reconstructed line is not a surveyed line.
The parked Brougham follows an 1893 catalogue while its owner and exact stop remain reconstructed. That exact design is too late to substantiate an 1871 vehicle.
Reuse urban rendering machinery; re-research 1871 parcels, materials, occupants, utilities, rails and plants.
The scene note saying only one building is stale; current compiled indexes contain 284 components.

year_audit.status: Planned door / superseded research date; no separate implemented scene
year_audit.summary: The 1880 URL is deliberately generated as a pending year. The 1888 representative date survives in research records after the Prairie Avenue target moved to 1904.
lessons: Do not count a navigable year URL as an existing reconstruction.
Do not treat a historical representative date as evidence that geometry exists for it.
For 1871, the grade-raise epoch is a placeholder ending 7 October; the postfire epoch starts 10 October. An 8 October pre-fire instant needs an explicit terrain/date decision.
Current 1904 ground must not be backdated to fill that gap.

lessons: The year slider filters known spans and nearby reference maps; it does not certify every selected day.

1830 plat: planned parcels and streets. The 1833 Conley–Stelzer map is a 1933 reconstruction. The 1834 Wright/Hathaway maps, 1836 Mesier map, 1839 harbor plan, 1849 Rees–Rucker map and 1853 Hart map have distinct purposes and dates.
1857 Palmatary and 1868 Ruger views help with appearance and massing, not measured footprint coordinates.
1870 Mitchell and four 1871 references support the near-fire study, but pre-fire views, city plans and burnt-district evidence must remain separate.
Preserve named structures separately from unnamed stock totals, and unknown fire fate as unknown.
Resolve addresses and georeference sources before claiming parcel placement.

readiness.title: Fix the date, hour and modeled extent
readiness.deliverable: An explicit October 8 pre-ignition scene specification, with a separate October 7 intact-city comparison if useful.
readiness.acceptance: Day, local time convention, bounding extent, Saturday Night Fire state and terrain interval agree; no scene is called rendered by this dossier.

readiness.title: Acquire and register primary sheets and photographs
readiness.deliverable: Verified map editions, uncropped image masters, 1871 directory and municipal-report page records.
readiness.acceptance: Every extracted attribute has a source, date, locator, access status and rights decision; catalog-only leads remain distinct from inspected pixels.

readiness.title: Build the 1871 ground state
readiness.deliverable: Georeferenced shoreline, lagoon, depot fill, river reaches, street grades, bridge/tunnel approaches and earlier-burn footprint.
readiness.acceptance: Control points and residuals recorded; terrain, water and walking heights agree; neither natural 1835 ground nor 1904 fill is silently reused.

readiness.title: Resolve physical building identities and date conflicts
readiness.deliverable: Dated parcel/structure register with original and replacement hotels, churches and institutions kept separate.
readiness.acceptance: Palmer conflict is ruled on or visibly unresolved; Nixon construction state and Crosby closure are honored; every included phase covers the cutoff.

readiness.title: Complete a landmark and an ordinary block
readiness.deliverable: Measured/reconstructed footprints, heights, roofs, openings, storefronts, rear buildings, yards and service access.
readiness.acceptance: Attribute-level confidence survives compilation; no anonymous citywide total is expanded into invented named buildings.

readiness.title: Prepare people and clothing evidence
readiness.deliverable: Household/business address joins, role inventory, comparative garment sheets and dated local image readings.
readiness.acceptance: Identity, presence, location, occupation, appearance and action confidence are separate; aggregate census counts never masquerade as street density.

readiness.title: Connect vehicles, paths and infrastructure
readiness.deliverable: Verified horsecar routes, omnibus transfers, dray/rail/boat types, bridge opening rules and stable support.
readiness.acceptance: Vehicle dates precede cutoff; dimensions and route provenance are explicit; no cable cars, elevated trains or later catalogue assets slip in.

readiness.title: Map plants, animals and October conditions
readiness.deliverable: Plantable habitat masks, cemetery/park phases, photographed trees, drought condition and independently sourced fauna.
readiness.acceptance: No mature proposed park or modern tree inventory; species, density, phenology and weather uncertainty remain exposed.

readiness.title: Author dated activity pilots
readiness.deliverable: Retail, waterfront and household pilots with actor–prop–place records and Sunday/hour constraints.
readiness.acceptance: Each motion has compatible paths and objects; documented activities remain separate from reconstructed timing, crowd density and named-person performance.

readiness.title: Review the reconstruction at street and city scale
readiness.deliverable: Named camera anchors, source-image comparisons, mobile/desktop checks, evidence cards and visible liberties.
readiness.acceptance: Zero missing assets or page errors, no terrain/footprint collisions, inspectable provenance, reproducible builds and an explicit list of unresolved gaps.
